In coming weeks, I plan to introduce the BIS Strength Act. It's legislation that'll prevent adversarial nations, certainly including China from acquiring a product that could boost their economic competitiveness in areas of concern, giving your Bureau the hiring authority to bring leading technologists in for 1-year terms at market competitive rates to craft smarter, faster policy.

Scam Alert: the IRS will not cold call you about back taxes.

As scams get more sophisticated — and use AI — these calls can sound legitimate. They’re still a scam.
The IRS typically starts with a letter in the mail. Even then, be cautious. If you need to follow up, only use contact information listed on https://t.co/Yh0PKB0R25 — not a number someone gives you over the phone.

As Chairman of the Congressional Stop Scams Caucus, I’m working to crack down on the criminals behind these schemes. Awareness is our best defense. #StopScams #IRS

Local communities should decide whether to approve a data center. The companies should pay for the power and grid upgrades they need—not shift those costs onto other customers. This week, I voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act to help protect Hoosiers from those added costs. Families and small businesses shouldn't be asked to foot the bill for big tech.

I’m reflecting this weekend on my visit last week in Washington with Archbishop Charles Thompson of the @archindy.

We discussed Pope Leo’s encyclical on artificial intelligence. I share his concern that technological progress must protect human dignity.

AI holds great promise — and challenges. Our responsibility is to guide its development with care for our families and the next generation.

I share these concerns. They relate to some of the concerns I spoke to with regard to financial scams committed against our citizens — many underpinned by rapidly developing AI technology. I think that our federal government should work to develop some guide rails on AI development and deployment broadly, and there ought to be honest conversation and deliberation over what we can attempt to regulate, or recognition of what we can't. But I think everyone in government — federal, state, and local — needs to be clear-eyed about the opportunity and the threat that burgeoning AI technology can present.
